players.note: Chuba Hubbard is Carolina's bell cow. Hubbard is the RB9 in fantasy points per game. Last week, he was the RB12 for the week. Hubbard finished with 23 touches and 110 total yards. Hubbard had an 83% snap rate, 82.6% of the rushing attempts, a 66.7% route share, and an 8.3% target share. Among 43 qualifying backs, he is 11th in explosive run rate and 14th in yards after contact per attempt. Hubbard should be a locked-in RB1 again this week. Detroit has allowed the highest explosive run rate, the 11th-highest rushing success rate, and the third-most yards before contact per attempt.

Aaron Jones is battling through a banged-up knee. Last week, despite the less-than-full-strength knee, Jones played 81.8% of the snaps with 73.9% of the rushing attempts, a 58.8% route share, and a 20.7% target share. Jones finished with 22 touches and 92 total yards. I don't know how long he'll hold up to this workload, but fantasy gamers should appreciate it while we have it. Among 43 qualifying rushers, Jones is 34th in explosive run rate, 37th in yards after contact per attempt, and 34th in missed tackle rate. None of those numbers surprise me at all. Jones is essentially Alvin Kamara of the North now. Jones is a volume-based RB2/flex again this week. Miami ranks 18th in explosive run rate, 17th in missed tackle rate, and has allowed the third-fewest yards before contact per attempt.

D'Andre Swift has been crushing it as the RB7 in fantasy points per game, averaging 20.7 touches and 107 total yards. Among 43 qualifying backs, Swift is eighth in yards after contact per attempt and tenth in missed tackle rate. Swift has 14 of the team's 20 running back red zone carries while playing 64.1% of the snaps with a 51.4% rushing share, a 35.7% route share, and a 9.2% target share. Swift should have another strong stat line this week against a Jets' run defense that has allowed the second-highest rushing success rate, the tenth-most yards before contact per attempt, and the third-highest missed tackle rate.

Cam Skattebo is the RB20 in fantasy points per game, averaging 19 touches and 78.3 total yards. Skattebo has a 65.7% snap rate, a 54.9% rushing share, a 48.9% route share, and a 9.6% target share. Among 43 qualifying backs, Skattebo ranks 19th in yards after contact per attempt and 12th in missed tackle rate. Skattebo should have another nice stat line this week. Arizona has allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the third-most yards after contact per attempt, and the second-highest missed tackle rate.

Bucky Irving picked up a glute injury in Week 3, but he looks good to go this week. He opened the week with limited practice sessions on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full on Friday. I expect Irving to handle his usual workload this week. In Weeks 1-2, Irving averaged 18 touches and 91.5 total yards with RB12 and RB15 finishes in weekly scoring. Among 43 qualifying backs, Irving ranks 18th in yards after contact per attempt and 15th in missed tackle rate. Irving should have a wonderful game against a run defense that has allowed the eighth-highest rushing success rate, the fifth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the highest yards per carry and rushing success rate to zone runs (Irving: 52.5% zone). Irving should feast this week as Tampa Bay could lean on him with Jalon Daniels making his first start.

Bhayshul Tuten is the RB16 in fantasy points per game, averaging 16 touches and 80 total yards. Among 42 qualifying running backs, he ranks tenth in explosive run rate, eighth in rushing success rate, tenth in yards after contact per attempt, and ninth in missed tackle rate. Among the same sample, Tuten is only 27th in snap rate and 24th in designed carry share. If he keeps producing like this on a per-touch basis, he will earn more of the Jags backfield. Tuten has six red zone carries to Chris Rodriguez's five through three games. He's had a consistent 31.3-35.5% route share (6.2% target share, 1.24 YPRR). This could be the week when Tuten finally logs a 100-yard rushing outing. Cincy has allowed the ninth-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the seventh-highest missed tackle rate.

Braelon Allen will be New York's lead back this week. Last week, Breece Hall sustained his quad injury in the fourth quarter. In the fourth quarter, Allen played 72% of the snaps with a 50% rushing share, a 52.6% route share, and a 17.6% target share. Allen has never been the most efficient rusher, and that is the case again this season. Allen has zero explosive runs, with 1.89 yards after contact per attempt and a 16% missed tackle rate. Allen could easily see 15-plus touches this week and return RB2 production despite his inefficiencies. Chicago hasn't been able to stop the run this season, allowing the ninth-highest explosive run rate, the highest rushing success rate, and the most yards before contact per attempt.

Well, this sucks. I expected David Montgomery to be Houston's workhorse back this season, and over the last two weeks that hasn't happened. Since Week 2, Montgomery has had a 57.8% snap rate with 43.6% of the rushing attempts, a 44.1% route share, and a 4.8% target share. In these two games, he has averaged 10.5 touches and 36 total yards. This is barely flex-worthy volume behind a horrid offensive line. Montgomery hasn't been efficient with his workload so far, though. He has only a 3% explosive run rate, 1.57 yards after contact per attempt, and a 14% missed tackle rate. None of that is good. At all. Montgomery has another nice matchup this week, but he wasn't able to do anything with last week's solid matchup, so I don't know if he'll be able to take advantage this week. Dallas has allowed the third-highest explosive run rate, the seventh-highest rushing success rate, and the eighth-most yards before contact per attempt.

Quinshon Judkins has been an uninspiring volume-based flex play as the RB29 in fantasy points per game. He has averaged 17 touches and 59 total yards. Among 42 qualifying rushers, Judkins has the seventh-lowest explosive run rate while ranking 29th in yards after contact per attempt and 21st in missed tackle rate. Judkins will put up another snoozer stat line this week against a Pittsburgh run defense that has the tenth-best stuff rate while allowing the seventh-lowest rushing success rate and the 12th-lowest missed tackle rate.

Alvin Kamara looks to be New Orleans' lead back while Travis Etienne is sidelined with a hamstring injury. Last week, after Etienne was out of the game in the fourth quarter, Kamara played 55% of the snaps, handled 71.4% of the rushing attempts, had a 46.2% route share, and zero targets. Kamara will be a volume play weekly. He hasn't been efficient or explosive this season with only a 5.6% explosive run rate, 1.78 yards after contact per attempt, and a 6% missed tackle rate. I expect Kendre Miller to work in on early downs so Kamara isn't asked to handle too many touches. Kamara is an unsexy volume flex this week with a bad matchup. Atlanta has allowed the lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest missed tackle rate, and the have the fourth-best stuff rate.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt is the RB34 in fantasy points per game, averaging 16.7 touches and 49 total yards. Bill has been a zero in the passing game with only one target in each game. He has five of the team's 11 running back red zone rushing attempts. Bill has a 47.2% snap rate with 49% of the team's rushing attempts, a 22.6% route share, and a 3% target share. All of his value in fantasy is tied to what he can do on early downs. Among 43 qualifying backs, he ranks 39th in explosive run rate, 35th in yards before contact per attempt, 31st in yards after contact per attempt, and 41st in missed tackle rate. His offensive line is giving him zero chances, as he has the second-highest rate of being hit at or behind the line of scrimmage. A porous Indy run defense might allow him some room to scamper this week. Indy has allowed the 11th-highest explosive run rate, the fourth-highest rushing success rate, the fifth-most yards before contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate. Bill is a solid flex play this week who could return RB2 value if he gets in the end zone.

Omarion Hampton has been a big letdown through three games as the RB23 in fantasy points per game. His usage trends are also going in a frightening direction, sadly. From Week 1 to last week, Hampton's designed carry share has dropped from 75% to 57.7%, and his route share has declined from 28.6% to 15.8%. There's nothing to like about any of that. Last week, Hampton finished with 15 touches and 56 total yards. In two of three games this season, he has had 15 touches or less. Among 43 qualifying backs, Hampton is 24th in explosive run rate, ninth in yards after contact per attempt, and 21st in missed tackle rate. With his route share declining and only a 3.4% target share this season, Hampton can easily be game-scripted out weekly if his usage continues to sit in this area code. That easily could happen this week against Seattle. The Seahawks' run defense also is no joke, as they have allowed the third-lowest explosive run rate, the third-lowest rushing success rate, and the sixth-lowest missed tackle rate. Hampton will need a touchdown to pay off this week for fantasy.

Last week, Rhamondre Stevenson was reinstalled as the team's lead back with a 55% snap rate and a 51.4% route share. Stevenson split the early down load with TreVeyon Henderson with a 26.9% rushing share, and each back got one red zone rushing attempt. Stevenson finished with ten touches and 38 total yards. Among 43 qualifying backs, Stevenson ranks 12th in yards after contact per attempt and 27th in missed tackle rate. Stevenson could take back more of the backfield this week if he can hold onto the ball. The Bills' run defense has been pliable, allowing the 12th-highest explosive run rate, the 12th-highest rushing success rate, and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate.

Well, after one game, TreVeyon Henderson returned to his 1B role in the New England backfield. Last week, Henderson finished with nine touches and 29 total yards while having a 33.3% snap rate, a 30.8% rushing share, and a 27% route share (3.2% target share). Henderson has gotten off to a disappointing start again this season on a per-touch basis. Among 43 qualifying backs, he is 27th in explosive run rate, 42nd in yards after contact per attempt, and 39th in missed tackle rate. It's not difficult to understand why Henderson can't seem to grasp or hold the lead back role in New England. Rhamondre Stevenson has been the better rusher over the last two seasons. Even in an ancillary role, Henderson is an interesting flex play this week. If he can pop one of his signature long runs for a touchdown, he could pay off this week. The Bills' run defense has been pliable, allowing the 12th-highest explosive run rate, the 12th-highest rushing success rate, and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate.

RJ Harvey remains Denver's passing-down back. In his two games of action this season, he has had a 42.1% snap rate, only 12.5% of the rushing attempts, a 44.1% route share, and a 17.7% target share (2.31 YPRR). Harvey has averaged 7.5 touches and 44 total yards. Harvey is a middling PPR flex again this week. The 49ers have allowed the ninth-most receiving fantasy points per game to backs, but they have also held them to the sixth-fewest yards per target.

Tony Pollard has taken over as Tennessee's lead back over the last two weeks. He has averaged 18 touches and 80.5 total yards while having a 53.7% snap share, 62% of the rushing attempts, a 33.3% route share, and an 8.9% target share. He's been stellar on a per-touch basis. Among 43 qualifying rushers, Pollard is ninth in explosive run rate and seventh in yards after contact per attempt. Last week, Pollard was the RB16 for the week. He could flirt with low-end RB2 production this week, but is best viewed as a nice flex play. Baltimore has allowed the sixth-highest explosive run rate, the 13th-most yards before contact per attempt, and the seventh-highest gap rushing success rate (Pollard: 65.8% gap runs).

Emanuel Wilson could lead the backfield this week in touches with Jadarian Price sidelined. Wilson has been their most trusted early down option so far this season with 40% of the rushing attempts, but he only has a 17.8% route share (George Holani, 29.7%). I expect Wilson to lead the way on early downs and in the rushing department while Holani handles passing downs and pass pro. Wilson has a below-average 1.97 yards after contact per attempt, but he has posted a strong 22% missed tackle rate. Wilson will need all the volume he can get this week against a run defense that has allowed the 11th-lowest explosive run rate, the fourth-lowest rushing success rate, and the 11th-fewest yards before contact per attempt and EPA per rush. Wilson could see 15 carries or more this week, though, and if he gets in the end zone, he could finish as a volume-drive RB2 or decent flex.

J.K. Dobbins remains Denver's early down hammer. In Weeks 1 and 3, Dobbins had a 46.7% snap rate, 62.5% of the rushing attempts, a 14.7% route share, and a 3.2% target share. In those games, he averaged 13 touches and 44.5 total yards. The biggest worry for Dobbins (outside of his touchdown-or-bust role) has been his inefficiency as a runner. Dobbins has only a 6.7% explosive run rate and a 6% missed tackle rate. These are horrible per-touch metrics for the explosive early down option for Denver. I don't see Dobbins improving those numbers this week. The 49ers have allowed the second-lowest explosive run rate, the sixth-fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the tenth-lowest missed tackle rate.

Woody Marks has made this Houston backfield into a committee. I didn't see that coming this offseason. Over the last two weeks, Marks has had a 41.4% snap rate, 33.3% of the rushing attempts, a 34.4% route share, and an 8.4% target share. Marks has averaged 9.5 touches and 28 total yards. Marks has had only 1.64 yards after contact per attempt, but he has also posted a stellar 27% missed tackle rate. Marks is a viable flex this week if you're in a pinch. Dallas has allowed the third-highest explosive run rate, the seventh-highest rushing success rate, and the eighth-most yards before contact per attempt.

Kyle Monangai is a serviceable flex again this week. Monangai has averaged 11.3 touches and 71 total yards while logging a 36.4% snap rate, 28.6% of the rushing attempts, a 26.1% route share, and a 4.1% target share. Monangai has six of 20 running back red zone carries for Chicago. Among 43 qualifying backs, he is first in yards after contact per attempt and 15th in missed tackle rate. The Jets have allowed the second-highest rushing success rate, the tenth-most yards before contact per attempt, and the third-highest missed tackle rate.

Jaylen Wright will be back this week, and I don't want to assume that Ollie Gordon will be Miami's workhorse even after his Week 3 showing. Wright has been the RB2 on the depth chart all summer and heading into the season. Both backs played only four snaps in Week 1 when they were both healthy, but Wright was the only one of the two of them to get a carry (one). Gordon, I think, could work in with Wright this week, but I'm expecting Wright to out-touch him. Wright is listed as the RB1 on the depth chart, currently. Gordon hasn't been efficient with the work he has seen going back to 2025. Since 2025 (90 carries), Gordon has only 1.84 yards after contact per attempt and an 8% missed tackle rate. I'm not flexing Gordon in this matchup. The Vikings have held backs to the second-lowest rushing success rate, the seventh-fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the 13th-lowest missed tackle rate.

Blake Corum is a low-end flex play again this week. Corum has averaged 10.3 touches and 53.3 total yards. He doesn't have a red zone carry so far this season, so his touchdown equity is limited at best. Also, he has only five targets this season, so his value is entirely dependent upon what he does on early downs and the possibility of him breaking off a long run for score. Corum has the talent to do so, but this isn't likely the best matchup for that to happen this week. Among 43 qualifying backs, Corum ranks fourth in explosive run rate and sixth in missed tackle rate. Philly's run defense has tightened up, allowing the 13th-lowest explosive run rate, the 12th-lowest rushing success rate, and the tenth-fewest yards before contact per attempt.

Bucky Irving missed part of Week 3's action with a glute injury. Irving opened this week with a limited practice session. I don't trust Todd Bowles and injury reporting. I'll update Kenneth Gainwell's outlook on Friday. If Irving misses this week, I would expect Gainwell to lead the way for the Bucs backfield.

Jaylen Wright missed last week's game with a foot injury. He opened this week with a limited practice on Wednesday. He had full practices on Thursday and Friday. He doesn't carry an injury designation into this week's game. I think Wright will play a prominent role in the Miami backfield this week. In Week 1, when both he and Ollie Gordon were healthy, Wright had four offensive snaps and a rushing attempt. Wright has been the RB2 on the depth chart entering the season and the more productive player than Gordon since 2025. He is currently listed as the RB1 on the depth chart over Gordon. Since 2025, among 60 qualifying backs, Wright has ranked 16th in rushing success rate, 18th in yards after contact per attempt, and ninth-best in missed tackle rate. Minnesota isn't a great matchup for Wright this week, though. The Vikings have held backs to the second-lowest rushing success rate, the seventh-fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the 13th-lowest missed tackle rate. Wright is only a deep league desperation flex this week.
